notes: The supplied Table 2/3 catalog is visibly truncated (T:p8-b0 and I:p8-b0; T:p8-b1 and I:p8-b1), so only the printed rows and IDs typed in text/figure labels can be listed; the remaining final candidates and the 6,673 substructure-unbound RRLs are reported only in aggregate (T:p5-b10; T:p6-b0) or in ID-less figures (T:p14-b5; I:p14-b0; I:p14-b1; I:p14-b2; I:p14-b3; I:p14-b4; I:p14-b5; T:p15-b0; I:p15-b0). Bronze Figure 2 sources Gaia DR3 378807525573579520, Gaia DR3 5337603936060261504, and Gaia DR3 4082164517027041920 remain candidates_found because the paper retains the 165 HV-RRL sample and treats bronze only as a reliability warning (T:p7-b2; T:p7-b4). Gaia DR3 3745877687375105408 and Gaia DR3 4055929177457043840 are included from the orbit-analysis discussion of HV-RRL candidates (T:p10-b5; T:p11-b4). Gaia DR3 3692326965681261184 is J1300+0256 and, with Gaia DR3 2644870582050682240 and Gaia DR3 3942539665718239360, is one of the three Prudil overlaps retained in this paper's classifications; they remain candidates_found. Gaia DR2 2471437298673558400 and Gaia DR2 1018414089653402496 are follow_up because the paper states they are prior Prudil candidates absent from the initial sample (T:p13-b0). Gaia DR3 3903031502808975616, Gaia DR3 674694939356598528, and Gaia DR3 3661050979472106880 are follow_up only because the current final selection excludes them via the velocity-uncertainty cut (T:p13-b0). Gaia DR3 3664033198603611520 is candidates_found: although it was a Prudil candidate and is omitted from the 165 field-star sample, the current paper calls it an unbound Sgr member and retains the substructure-unbound population (T:p5-b10; T:p13-b0).

Gaia DR3 378807525573579520: The target is the first row of Table 2 (T:p8-b0): Gaia ID 378807525573579520, catalog L23, light-curve quality bronze. Table 2 reports v_GC,t = 1530.9 ± 171.5 km s^-1, explicitly the tangential Galactic-rest-frame velocity component, not the total three-dimensional speed; because no total Galactic-rest-frame velocity or radial velocity is reported for this star in Table 2, it was not mapped to galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Table 3 (T:p8-b1) reports only unbound probabilities under six potential models; no bound probabilities are reported.

Gaia DR3 4918733303434183296: Target star Gaia DR3 4918733303434183296 is the second row of Table 2 (L23 catalog, silver quality light curve). Table 2 reports tangential Galactic rest-frame velocity v_GC,t = 549.9 ± 127.1 km/s rather than a total v_GC, and no radial velocity is available for this star, so no radial_velocity or galactic_rest_frame_velocity is recorded. Table 3 gives unbound probabilities under six potential models; all are reported separately since the paper does not select a single preferred model. The paper reports no parallax for this star (distances come from the RR Lyrae period-metallicity relation, not parallax).

Gaia DR3 4717299539114264320: The target is a gold-sample HV-RRL. T:p7-b7 states that none of the gold and silver HV-RRL candidates have measured radial velocities, so no radial_velocity is retained. Table 2 reports v_GC,t (tangential velocity), not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed; accordingly, no total galactic_rest_frame_velocity is retained. Table 3 reports P_unb for six potential models.

Gaia DR3 4910044167981920384: Target Gaia DR3 4910044167981920384 is the Table 2 entry in T:p8-b0 (L23, gold). Table 2 reports tangential Galactic rest-frame velocity v_GC,t = 369.1 ± 99.4 km/s, not total 3D Galactic rest-frame speed, and no radial velocity is reported for this star in the supplied text; therefore galactic_rest_frame_velocity is not extracted. Table 3 (T:p8-b1) reports P_unb under several potential models; bound probabilities are not reported and were not computed.

Gaia DR3 4936275766641005312: Table 2 (T:p8-b0) lists v_GC,t = 462.0 ± 102.3 km/s for the target, but this is a tangential velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed. The target is in the gold sample, and Section 3.1 (T:p7-b7) states that none of the gold/silver HV-RRL candidates have measured radial velocities; therefore no radial_velocity or total galactic_rest_frame_velocity value was extracted. Table 3 (T:p8-b1) reports unbound probabilities under the listed potential models.

Gaia DR3 2004005081455404416: The target appears in Table 2 as a bronze-quality HV-RRL candidate and in Table 3 for unbound probabilities (T:p8-b0, T:p8-b1). Table 2 reports only the tangential Galactic rest-frame velocity v_GC,t = 474.6 ± 67.7 km/s for this star, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No parallax or radial velocity is reported for this target in the supplied material.

Gaia DR3 2644870582050682240: Target Gaia DR3 2644870582050682240 is a W22 HV-RRL candidate classified as "bronze" in Table 2; the paper cautions that bronze-sample light curves, hence distances/velocities, are less reliable. Table 2 reports only the tangential Galactic rest-frame velocity v_GC,t, not the total 3D v_GC; I record that tangential value under galactic_rest_frame_velocity with that condition because no total velocity is reported. No radial velocity or parallax for this target is given in the supplied text/table.

Gaia DR3 2215178865230742912: Target Gaia DR3 2215178865230742912 appears in Table 2 as a gold-quality HV-RRL candidate from L23. Its Table 2 velocity is the tangential Galactic-rest-frame velocity v_GC,t = 410.8 ± 93.3 km/s, not the total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed, so galactic_rest_frame_velocity was not extracted. The paper states that none of the gold and silver candidates have measured radial velocities, so radial_velocity was not extracted. Table 3 P_unb values are reported as unbound probabilities under the listed potential models; bound_probability is not separately reported.

Gaia DR3 6522342764544281856: Target is Gaia DR3 6522342764544281856, an RR Lyrae (L23 catalog, gold light-curve quality) among the 165 HV-RRL candidates; it appears in the last row of the printed Table 2 and Table 3. It has no measured radial velocity, so only the tangential Galactic rest-frame velocity v_GC,t = 462.8 ± 111.4 km/s (Table 2) is reported; since this is a tangential component rather than the total three-dimensional speed, it is not entered as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No parallax is given (distances come from the period-metallicity relation). Bound probabilities are not reported separately, only P_unb. The six P_unb values derive from the six potential models of Table 3.

Gaia DR3 6343475759127147008: The target (Gaia DR3 6343475759127147008) is listed in Table 2 as a gold-sample HV-RRL candidate from L23. Table 2 reports a Galactic rest-frame tangential velocity v_GC,t = 383.9 ± 66.1 km/s; this is not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, and the star has no radial-velocity measurement in the paper, so it is not entered as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No parallax is reported for this star (its distance comes from the RRL period–metallicity relation). In Table 3, the unbound probabilities for the six potential models are given in the row order Bovy15, Cautun20, Monari18, McMillan17, Irrgang13I, Bovy15+LMC.

Gaia DR3 5337603936060261504: The target, Gaia DR3 5337603936060261504, appears in the supplied material only as one of three example light curves of the "bronze" (doubtful) sample in Figure 2 (I:p7-b1): source ID 5337603936060261504, type = RRc, N = 50, p = 0.3553 day. The caption (T:p7-b2) describes this middle panel: "The middle panel shows a steep rise and an amplitude exceeding 0.8 mag, suggesting it should be classified as an RRab rather than an RRc." No right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this specific star anywhere in the supplied text or images: it is not among the rows of Table 2 (T:p8-b0/I:p8-b0) or Table 3 (T:p8-b1/I:p8-b1), which present only a partial listing ("......") of the 165 candidates, with the complete table available online. Therefore no eligible quantities could be extracted for this star. The light-curve period, amplitude, and magnitude data are not among the requested quantities.

Gaia DR3 4082164517027041920: The target Gaia DR3 4082164517027041920 appears only in the light-curve figure as a bronze-sample RRc star (I:p7-b2; see also T:p7-b2). The supplied material reports no values for the requested quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for this star.

Gaia DR3 3745877687375105408: The target Gaia DR3 3745877687375105408 is mentioned only at T:p10-b5, where the paper reports a 19.0% probability that its backward-integrated minimum distance reached within 1 kpc of the Galactic Center. This is an origin-probability result, not one of the eligible requested quantities (such as bound/unbound probability). The supplied excerpt of Table 2 and Table 3 does not include this star, so no eligible position, distance, velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is available in the supplied material.

Gaia DR3 4055929177457043840: The target Gaia DR3 4055929177457043840 is mentioned only at T:p11-b4. The paper states that its backward-integrated minimum distance falls within the half-light radius of the Sgr dwarf galaxy (2.6 kpc), with probabilities 41.9%, 40.9%, and 37.4% under the three assumed radial-velocity distributions. Those probabilities are not bound/unbound probabilities, and 2.6 kpc is the Sgr half-light radius, not the star's Galactocentric radius. No individual RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star in the supplied material; Table 2 is truncated and does not include this ID.

J1300+0256: Target J1300+0256 is identified as Gaia DR3 3692326965681261184, an RRc-type star in the silver sample. The supplied Table 2 is only a partial listing and does not include the target row, so its tabulated RA, Dec, proper motion, distance, R_GC, v_GC,t, and P_unb values are not available. Section 4.1 gives no numerical refined heliocentric distance or parallax. The Hα radial velocity 163.6 ± 12.2 km/s is the observed value before the reported pulsation correction; the paper reports a correction of 29.1 ± 4.5 km/s but does not state an explicit corrected radial velocity, so no corrected value was calculated or recorded. The quoted R = 39.50 kpc is interpreted as Galactocentric radius based on the paper’s escape-velocity context. No numerical bound or unbound probability is reported for this star in the supplied material.

Gaia DR3 3942539665718239360: The target star Gaia DR3 3942539665718239360 is mentioned only in Section 4.2 (T:p13-b0) as one of three stars overlapping with Prudil et al. (2022); there it is stated that the three overlap stars fall into the gold, silver, and bronze categories, respectively, implying this star is in the gold sample. No individual numerical values for right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability are reported for this star in the supplied text or in the provided excerpts of Table 2 and Table 3 (which list only a subset of candidates and do not include this Gaia ID).

(2022) candidates not included in the authors' initial sample. The paper reports no position, distance, parallax, proper-motion, velocity, Galactocentric-radius, or bound/unbound probability values for this star.

(2022) candidates that “are not included in our initial sample.” The supplied material provides no position, distance, parallax, proper-motion, velocity, probability, or other quantitative values for this star.
